claim:s1-metabolic-partnership.proposition: An archaeal-bacterial association can become mutually beneficial under restricted redox and substrate regimes — a connected cross-feeding community develops functional redundancy that an isolated (no-exchange) control does not, on mass-balanced exchange — but the benefit is not necessarily stable or obligate and disappears outside the feasible regime.
claim:s1-metabolic-partnership.hypothesis: Under at least one field-consistent redox/substrate regime, a reconstructed archaeal-host / bacterial-partner pair achieves partner-dependent growth (each grows better together than alone) on mass-balanced exchange fluxes, while a no-exchange / parasitic control does not.

provenance.note: Calibrated at p_diacid=1e-8, p_monoacid=1e-7, k_wash=0.01, 250 steps (og-07 nominal): the connected arm (coupling=shared) settles to 0.536 (PASS) while the isolated control (coupling=private, the `isolated-control` variant) settles to 0.464 (FAIL) — a partner-dependent advantage of connected/isolated = 1.15. A majority of capabilities are redundantly covered only with cross-feeding.
Exchange fluxes must conserve carbon; worst-case C residual stays ~0 (observed 5.6e-11).

claim:s2-ecology-to-proximity.proposition: Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (low-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding flux is strongly distance-dependent — proximate (mixed) partners sustain the exchange while distant (segregated) partners lose it — creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis. The advantage vanishes under high diffusion (well-mixed), so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.
claim:s2-ecology-to-proximity.hypothesis: Below a critical diffusion length the cross-feeding flux is distance-dependent and selects for sustained contact; under well-mixed (high-diffusion) conditions the proximity advantage collapses, so selection for contact is a spatial-structure effect, not a given.

provenance.note: Calibrated at p_diacid=1e-8, p_monoacid=1e-7, k_wash=0.01, k_diffusion=0.001, 250 steps: mixed (proximate) settles to 4.0e-22 (PASS) while the segregated control (the `distant-control` variant) settles to 1.8e-23 (FAIL) — a 22x proximity advantage. Under high diffusion (k_diffusion=0.1) the mixed/segregated ratio falls to 1.26: the advantage vanishes well-mixed.

claim:s3-protrusions-to-enclosure.proposition: Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit (S1/S2): observed protrusion mechanics can, under favorable area and adhesion budgets, reach stable wrapping over a majority of the partner-size range — but a beneficial symbiosis need not imply ingestive ability, and enclosure fails without wrapping (no-enclosure) or when adhesion cannot pay the bending cost.
claim:s3-protrusions-to-enclosure.hypothesis: Under cryo-ET-constrained bending moduli and adhesion, at least one topology (classical engulfment or inside-out wrapping) reaches a stable enclosed state over a realistic partner-size range with conserved membrane area, while a no-enclosure or weak-adhesion control does not.

provenance.note: Calibrated (classical engulfment, protrusion_area=4 um^2, adhesion=600 kT, kappa=20 kT, 30 steps): enclosure_probability settles to 0.61 (PASS; inside-out wrapping reaches 0.98). Two failure routes read 0.0: the no-enclosure control and the weak-adhesion control (adhesion below the 8*pi*kappa bending cost).
Area conservation under bending (residual ~0 by construction).

claim:s4-compartmental-energetic-couplin.proposition: An enclosed partner may develop organelle-like function only under restricted physiological conditions: internalization yields a net energetic benefit (the population internalizes gradient generation and persists) solely where the pump is efficient; there exist regimes (a weak pump) where internalization cannot pay the membrane cost and the population collapses.
claim:s4-compartmental-energetic-couplin.hypothesis: Internalization is net-positive only in a restricted regime: where the pump is efficient enough to internalize gradient generation before the external gradient collapses. Outside that regime (a weak pump) the population cannot pay the Sojo membrane cost and collapses.

provenance.note: Calibrated (catalyst_efficiency=1.0, v_start=0.40, decline_rate=0.01, gradient_floor=0.02, 60 steps): survivors settle to 1.00 (PASS; internalization 0.95, autonomy 0.99, lineage fitness 0.68). The weak-pump control (catalyst_efficiency=0.3, the `weak-pump-control` variant) collapses to survivors 0.00 (FAIL; fitness 0.059) — the harmful regime.

claim:s5-symbiont-to-organelle.proposition: Integration becomes heritable and coordinated — a new evolutionary individual emerges — only when vertical-transmission fidelity crosses the Eigen error threshold, after which the inherited phenotype persists with function across generations. Below threshold (low-fidelity template) the lineage hits the error catastrophe and collapses; a non-heritable mechanism transmits nothing.
claim:s5-symbiont-to-organelle.hypothesis: Stable heritable integration requires high-fidelity vertical transmission: only above the Eigen error threshold does the inherited phenotype persist with function across generations. Below threshold (low fidelity) the lineage collapses; without an inheritance mechanism (non-heritable) there is no vertical transmission at all.

provenance.note: Calibrated (module=template, per_site_fidelity=0.99, 60 steps): heritability settles to 0.989 (PASS; functional fraction 1.0, population 220, lineage depth 60). Two failure routes fall below 0.95 — a low-fidelity template (per_site_fidelity=0.80, the `low-fidelity-control` variant) hits the Eigen error catastrophe (heritability 0.799, functional fraction 0.0, population 0), and the non-heritable control reads 0.106.

narrative.question: Under what physical, metabolic, ecological, and evolutionary conditions can a symbiotic association between an archaeal host and a bacterial partner transition into an integrated eukaryotic cell? The aim is not to animate a predetermined history but to identify plausible, impossible, and still-unresolved pathways from ecological association to a new evolutionary individual.

units.proposition: An archaeal-bacterial association can become mutually beneficial under restricted redox and substrate regimes — a connected cross-feeding community develops functional redundancy that an isolated (no-exchange) control does not, on mass-balanced exchange — but the benefit is not necessarily stable or obligate and disappears outside the feasible regime.

Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (low-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding flux is strongly distance-dependent — proximate (mixed) partners sustain the exchange while distant (segregated) partners lose it — creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis. The advantage vanishes under high diffusion (well-mixed), so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.

Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit (S1/S2): observed protrusion mechanics can, under favorable area and adhesion budgets, reach stable wrapping over a majority of the partner-size range — but a beneficial symbiosis need not imply ingestive ability, and enclosure fails without wrapping (no-enclosure) or when adhesion cannot pay the bending cost.

An enclosed partner may develop organelle-like function only under restricted physiological conditions: internalization yields a net energetic benefit (the population internalizes gradient generation and persists) solely where the pump is efficient; there exist regimes (a weak pump) where internalization cannot pay the membrane cost and the population collapses.

Integration becomes heritable and coordinated — a new evolutionary individual emerges — only when vertical-transmission fidelity crosses the Eigen error threshold, after which the inherited phenotype persists with function across generations. Below threshold (low-fidelity template) the lineage hits the error catastrophe and collapses; a non-heritable mechanism transmits nothing.

decisions.title: Which two or more candidate archaeal-host / bacterial-partner genome pairs anchor S1 (e.g. Asgard + alphaproteobacterium selections from GTDB/NCBI), and under which redox / substrate regimes (anaerobic, micro-aerobic) are they first tested?
decisions.detail: No single extant isolate is the ancestral host; S1 must reconstruct two or more pairs with explicit uncertainty rather than pick one.

decisions.title: Which initial ecology (syntrophy, commensalism, parasitism) is the primary scenario for S2, and which are the competing scenarios run head to head?
decisions.detail: Section 7 requires testing alternative initial ecologies, not assuming syntrophy.
